India's elephant population concentrated in a handful of strongholds, led by Karnataka and Assam

Elephant numbers are concentrated in a few strongholds: Karnataka (6,013) and Assam (4,159) alone hold nearly half of India's 22,446 estimated elephants. The Western Ghats and NE Hills & Brahmaputra landscapes dominate overall, while Shivalik Hills & Gangetic Plains rests almost entirely on Uttarakhand (1,792). Central India & Eastern Ghats is the most fragmented, spread thinly across seven states with none exceeding 1,000.
